name: Russell's Viper
len: 1-1.5 m, large ones to about 1.8 m
habitat: Open scrub, grassland, farmland, rocky ground and plantations where rats are plentiful; avoids dense forest and true desert
range: Most of India except the far north-east and high Himalaya; also Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Nepal and Bangladesh
diet: Rodents mainly, plus lizards, frogs, scorpions and crabs
active: Mostly nocturnal; rests under bushes or in grass by day
ids: Three rows of large dark oval spots with black-and-white rims run down the back and flanks on a tan, brown or yellowish body, like a chain.
Broad, triangular head, clearly wider than the thin neck, with a pale V- or X-shaped mark on top.
Thick, heavy body with rough, keeled scales that tapers quickly into a short tail.
Large eyes with vertical, slit-like pupils and big, obvious nostrils.
Coils into an S-shape and gives a long, sustained hiss, one of the loudest of any snake, before striking.

look.pattern: Chain of three rows of dark, white-ringed oval spots
look.head: Large triangular head with a pale V mark and big nostrils
look.body: Thick and heavy, rough scales, short tail

fact: Russell's Viper causes many bites on farms because it lies motionless in grass and is easily trodden on. It gives birth to live young, up to several dozen at a time.

name: Saw-scaled Viper
habitat: Dry sandy and rocky country: scrub, dunes, dry forest and farmland; hides under stones, logs and in crevices
range: Dry parts of peninsular India, the Deccan, Rajasthan and Gujarat and coastal sand and laterite plateaus; absent from wet evergreen forest and the north-east
diet: Scorpions, centipedes, lizards, frogs and small rodents
active: Mainly nocturnal; may be active by day when it is cloudy
ids: Small, stout snake with rough, strongly keeled scales. When threatened it rubs its coils together to make a hissing, sawing sound.
A pale cross, arrow or trident mark on top of a broad, pear-shaped head that is clearly wider than the neck.
Sandy, brown, grey or reddish body with a row of pale blotches along the back and a wavy white line along each flank.
Large eyes with vertical pupils and a short, stubby tail.
Often rests in a tight C-shaped or figure-of-eight coil with the head in the middle.

look.pattern: Pale blotches down the back, wavy white line on each side, pale cross on the head
look.head: Broad, pear-shaped head wider than the neck

fact: Despite its small size, the Saw-scaled Viper is blamed for more deaths than any other snake in many dry regions, because it is so common and so easily stepped on.

name: Hump-nosed Pit Viper
habitat: Leaf litter in wet forest, plantations (rubber, coffee, arecanut, tea), gardens and stream banks in the Western Ghats and the coastal strip below
range: Western Ghats and coastal Karnataka, Goa, Kerala and Tamil Nadu; also Sri Lanka
diet: Lizards, frogs, skinks and small rodents
active: Nocturnal and active at dusk; rests coiled in leaf litter by day
ids: Small, stout snake with an upturned, hump-like tip to the snout. The snub nose gives it a pug-like profile.
Brown, reddish-brown, grey or pinkish body with dark triangles or blotches down the back and a pale, mottled belly.
Broad triangular head, thin neck, vertical pupils and a heat-sensing pit between the eye and the nostril.
Rough, keeled scales; usually found coiled among dead leaves, so it blends in superbly.
Easily mistaken for a harmless snake, but its bite causes severe tissue damage and can injure the kidneys.

look.colour: Brown, rusty or greyish; paler belly
look.pattern: Dark triangles or blotches along the back
look.head: Triangular head with an upturned, hump-like snout

fact: Hump-nosed pit vipers are often killed or ignored because they are small and drab, yet their bites are a serious problem in the Western Ghats. There is no specific antivenom for them.

name: Malabar Pit Viper
habitat: Evergreen and moist forest, shola edges and plantations in hills, usually on low branches, rocks or tree trunks
range: Western Ghats from Maharashtra and Goa south through Karnataka and Kerala
diet: Lizards, frogs, birds and small rodents
ids: Wildly variable colour: bright green, yellow, olive, brown, orange, pinkish or blue-grey, often mottled with dark or white blotches. Colour alone does not identify it.
Stout-bodied for a tree viper, with a broad, flat, triangular head and a blunt snout.
Vertical pupils and a heat-sensing pit between the eye and the nostril; rough, keeled scales.
Short, slightly grasping tail. Waits coiled on a low branch or rock, often at head height beside a forest path.
A pit viper of the Western Ghats hills and nowhere else in India.

look.colour: Green, yellow, brown, orange or grey; extremely variable
look.pattern: Plain or marbled; dark and pale blotches on many
look.head: Broad, flat triangular head with a blunt snout
look.body: Stout with keeled scales and a short tail

fact: One of the most colourful snakes in India: single litters of Malabar Pit Vipers can contain green, brown and even orange babies.

name: Bamboo Pit Viper
habitat: Forest, bamboo clumps, scrub, plantations and gardens, in bushes and on low branches
range: Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats and much of peninsular India south of the Gangetic plain
diet: Lizards, frogs, small birds and rodents
ids: Slim, bright grass-green snake (some individuals yellow) with a lighter, yellowish or white line along the lowest row of scales on each side.
Flat, triangular head, much wider than the neck, with a yellow-green lip and golden-yellow eyes with vertical pupils.
A heat-sensing pit between the eye and nostril; keeled scales and a short tail that may have a reddish or yellow tip.
Climbs bushes and bamboo and loops over twigs, often found at eye level.

look.colour: Bright green, sometimes yellowish; yellow lip
look.pattern: Plain, with a pale line along each flank
look.head: Flat triangular head with golden eyes and a pit
look.body: Slim for a viper, with keeled scales and a short tail

fact: Green pit vipers are well camouflaged but give themselves away with a triangular head and vertical pupils, two things a green vine snake does not have.

name: Anamalai Pit Viper
habitat: High-altitude evergreen forest and shola, on branches and tree trunks
range: Higher hills of the southern Western Ghats (Anamalai, Palni, Nelliampathy and neighbouring ranges in Kerala and Tamil Nadu)
ids: Stocky, mottled pit viper in olive-brown, yellow-brown, orange-brown or greenish tones, with dark speckles and blotches.
Broad triangular head with a rounded snout, vertical pupils and a pit between eye and nostril.
Found only in the high hills of the southern Western Ghats, usually coiled on a branch.

look.pattern: Dark speckles and blotches, often marbled
look.head: Broad triangular head, rounded snout

fact: This pit viper lives only in a small area of high hills in the southern Western Ghats.

name: Large-scaled Pit Viper
habitat: Montane evergreen forest, shola and plantations, in shrubs and on low branches
range: High ranges of the southern Western Ghats (Kerala and Tamil Nadu)
ids: Bright green pit viper with noticeably large, overlapping scales that give a coarse, mosaic-like texture.
Yellow-white stripe along the lips and often along the lower flank; golden eyes with vertical pupils.
Triangular head, heat-sensing pit and a short prehensile tail that can be reddish.
Looks almost the same as the Bamboo Pit Viper; range and scale size separate them.

look.colour: Bright green with a yellow-white lip line
look.head: Triangular head with large head scales
look.body: Slim to medium, with big keeled scales

fact: The 'large-scaled' in its name is real: its dorsal scales are bigger than those of the other green pit vipers of the Western Ghats.

name: Travancore Pit Viper
habitat: Evergreen forest and stream sides in the hills, on rocks, logs and low vegetation
range: Southern Western Ghats of Kerala and Tamil Nadu
ids: Brown, olive or greenish-grey pit viper with darker mottling and blotches, and a dark streak behind the eye.
Broad triangular head, vertical pupils and a heat-sensing pit between the eye and nostril.
Rough keeled scales and a short tail; found on rocks and low branches near forest streams.

look.head: Broad triangular head with a dark eye streak

name: Red-tailed Bamboo Pit Viper
habitat: Bushes, bamboo, hedges, mangroves, tea gardens and village edges in damp lowlands
range: West Bengal (including the Sundarbans), Assam, Tripura, Mizoram and neighbouring north-eastern states; also Bangladesh
diet: Frogs, lizards, small birds and rodents
ids: Slender, leaf-green snake with a reddish or brown tail tip and a pale yellow-white stripe along each side.
Triangular head, golden-yellow or orange eyes with vertical pupils and a heat-sensing pit.
Keeled scales, thin neck and a prehensile tail; coils on bushes and bamboo.
The common green pit viper of north-eastern India and the Bengal delta.

look.colour: Bright green with a red-brown tail tip
look.pattern: Plain; yellow-white stripe on each side
look.head: Triangular head with golden eyes and a pit
look.body: Slim, keeled, with a prehensile tail

fact: This green pit viper is common on tea estates and in village hedgerows, where careless hands can meet it among the foliage.

name: Salazar's Pit Viper
habitat: Forest and scrub in hill areas, in bushes and low trees
range: Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and the hills of West Bengal
diet: Frogs, lizards, small birds and rodents
ids: Green to yellow-green pit viper, often noticeably yellowish, with a pale stripe along the lips.
Triangular head, golden eyes with vertical pupils and a heat-sensing pit.
Slim body with keeled scales and a prehensile tail, sometimes with a reddish tip.
One of several north-eastern green pit vipers that look nearly identical, so range matters.

look.colour: Green to yellow-green; pale lip stripe
look.head: Triangular head with golden eyes

name: Pope's Pit Viper
habitat: Hill forest, bamboo and shrubs near streams
range: Hills of north-eastern India (Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram) and eastwards
diet: Frogs, lizards, birds and small mammals
ids: Green pit viper with a pale (often white and red) stripe along each side in males, and a reddish tail.
Triangular head, reddish or orange eyes, vertical pupils and a heat-sensing pit.
Keeled scales and a prehensile tail; often coiled on a streamside branch.

look.colour: Green with a pale side stripe
look.pattern: Plain; white-and-red side stripe in males
look.head: Triangular head with a pit

name: Himalayan White-lipped Pit Viper
habitat: Hill forest, scrub and farm edges at low to middle elevations, in bushes and on rocks
range: Western Himalayan foothills (Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Jammu & Kashmir) and Nepal
ids: Green pit viper with a conspicuous white or yellowish stripe along the upper lip and often along the flank.
Triangular head, vertical pupils and a heat-sensing pit; keeled scales.
The green pit viper of the western Himalayan foothills.

look.colour: Green with a white or yellow lip stripe
look.head: Triangular head with a pit

name: Andaman Pit Viper
habitat: Forest, plantations and gardens on the islands, on branches and the ground
range: Andaman and Nicobar Islands (the only pit viper found there)
ids: Stocky pit viper in brown, olive or grey with darker blotches or marbling; some are plain dark brown.
Broad triangular head, vertical pupils and a heat-sensing pit.
The only pit viper on the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, so locality is a strong clue.

look.pattern: Dark blotches or marbling, sometimes plain
look.head: Broad triangular head with a pit

name: Himalayan Pit Viper
habitat: Rocky slopes, scrub, forest edges and farmland at 1,500 to 4,000 m, often basking on stone walls and paths
range: Western Himalaya: Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, extending into Nepal and Pakistan
diet: Lizards, frogs, small rodents and insects
active: By day in cool weather, evening in warm weather
ids: Stout, short snake in brown, grey-brown or coppery tones with dark blotches or a zigzag along the back.
Broad, triangular head, vertical pupils and a heat-sensing pit; no hood.
Lives at high altitude in the western Himalaya, an area where few other dangerous snakes occur.

look.pattern: Dark blotches or zigzag along the back
look.head: Broad triangular head with a pit

fact: Few snakes live as high as this one. It gives birth to live young because eggs would not survive the cold.

name: Mountain Pit Viper
habitat: Hill and mountain forest, among leaf litter, rocks and moss, often by streams
range: Eastern Himalaya and the hills of north-eastern India (Sikkim, West Bengal hills, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Nagaland)
ids: Stout brown or grey-brown snake with large dark squarish blotches along the back, often in an alternating pattern.
Broad, flat triangular head with a dark streak behind the eye; vertical pupils and a pit.
Rough keeled scales; sits coiled in leaf litter or on a mossy log in hill forest.

look.pattern: Large dark squarish blotches along the back
look.head: Broad flat triangular head with a dark eye streak

name: Jerdon's Pit Viper
habitat: Hill forest, scrub and rocky slopes
range: Hills of Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and Manipur, and eastwards into Myanmar and China
ids: Olive-brown to greyish snake with a row of dark, yellow-edged blotches or rings down the back.
Slender, elongated triangular head, vertical pupils and a heat-sensing pit.
Slimmer than most pit vipers in the region and found only in the far north-eastern hills.

look.pattern: Dark, yellow-edged blotches down the back
look.head: Elongated triangular head with a pit
